tossups.text: The Nika Riots broke out in a venue in which these vehicles were raced. Muwatalli II led a force of thousands of these vehicles in the 1274 BCE Battle of Kadesh, the largest battle of these in history. The largest venue for racing these vehicles was built across the Palatine Hill from the Colosseum in Rome. Hippodromes and the Circus Maximus hosted races of, for 10 points, what two-wheeled horse-drawn carts?

South of the city of Kielce, this man led his twelve thousand troops and defeated the twenty-four thousand troops led by Augustus II the Strong at the Battle of Kliszow. However in Ukraine, this ruler's general Adam Ludwig Lewenhaupt surrendered twelve thousand troops to Alexander Menshikov at Perevolochna. In Estonia, eight thousand five hundred troops led by Carl Gustav Rehnskiold who assisted this ruler defeated thirty-seven troops led by Charles Eugene de Croy at one battle. This ruler escaped to the Turkish fortresses located at Bender, Moldava, when again in Ukraine, forces outnumbered two to one led by Rehnskiold and Ivan Mazepa would be defeated. Victorious at the Battle of Narva but defeated at the Battle of Poltava, for 10 points, name this king of Sweden defeated by Russia's Peter I during the Great Northern War.

In human physiology, this structure is essential for ascending and descending tracts. It plays a key role in the nervous system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this spinal cord-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The spinal cord is a key component of the Nervous system, involved in ascending and descending tracts.

tossups.text: This literary character is mistaken for the housemaid Mary Ann by a creature who employs Bill the Lizard to get this character out of his house. This character is transformed by a fan, mushrooms, and magical cakes marked "EAT ME" after following a White Rabbitinto a land inhabited by Tweedle-Dee, Tweedle-Dum, and the Cheshire Cat. For ten points, name the little girl created by Lewis Carroll who goes on adventures in Wonderland.

This river's 4000 Islands are downstream from the city of Pakse, and phosphine gas may be the cause of mysterious Naga fireballs that rise from it. This river drains the Khorat Plateau via the Mun and Chi rivers, and its upper portion is made unnavigable by the Khone ["koh-nay"] Falls. In the Hengduan Mountains of Yunnan Province, this river flows parallel to the Salween and Yangtze ["yant-see"], and it is home to a species of giant catfish. This river flows through Vientiane and Phnom Penh ["fenom pen"]. For 10 points, name this river that empties into the South China Sea in southern Vietnam.
acceptableAnswers: any of the near infinite local names for it if anyone decides to show off

tossups.text: One of this composer's works includes tubular bells during the break strain. Another of his works counters trombones and tubas with a trio featuring piccolos, and was honored by Congress in 1987. His "Washington Post" earned this director of the US Marine Band the nickname the "March King." For 10 points, name composer of the "Liberty Bell," whose "The Stars and Stripes Forever" is America's National March.

Only two photographs of this religion's founder are known to exist, which are infrequently viewed when not on pilgrimage. A Guardian of this religion attempted to expand it during the Ten Year World Crusade. One text of this religion observed by Shoghi Effendi was written in response to questions from two prominent Sufis and is titled The Seven Valleys, and this religion has a nineteen-month calendar consisting of nineteen days each. Another text of this religion symbolized by a nine-pointed star is The Book of Certitude. For 10 points, name this religion governed from the Universal House of Justice, which was founded by the Báb and Bahá'u'lláh.

This country's primary instruments are the lingm flute, two-string chiwang bowed fiddle, and a narrow lute that has three doubled courses, an optional high ting ti string, and an ornately carved colorful headstock shaped like the chusin sea monster to repel evil spirits. Though shared with people to the north, zhey and zhem are paired Cham dances celebrated in this country's Tsechu festivals. Glu is a folksong genre from this country, which developed a fast-paced pop style in the late 1960s called rigsar that uses synthesizers and a modernized metal-stringed dranyen lute. For 10 points, the ceremonial dungkar conch, traditional music styles zhungdra and bödra, and musicologist Jigme Drukpa are from what country?

In this body of water, the theme park Blackgang Chine can be found on an island that hosts a garlic festival in the town of Ryde. Jersey and Guernsey cows are native to islands in this body of water which is also home to the Isle of Wight. The culturally Gallic regions of Cornwall and Brittany are separated by this body of water. Traversing this body of water is a notable solo swimming feat, but many travelers use its namesake tunnel instead to cross from Folkestone to Calais. For 10 points, name this body of water which separates France and the United Kingdom.

A class of alkylating agents including carboquone and ThioTEPA contain this functionality, which can be synthesized from vinyl dihalides and DBU in a reaction named for Cromwell and Gabriel. One method of synthesizing these compounds involves the [3+2] addition of a guanidinium ylide to carbonyl compounds. Leighton and Rhenquist modified one important method of synthesizing these compounds by lowering the temperature and adding glass beads, while another method was modified to use LiAl4 instead of a Grignard reaction. That method has an "intermolecular trapping" variant developed by Taguchi and begins with a ketoxime, known as the Hoch-Campbell reaction. A more popular method of synthesizing them uses sulfuric acid on a beta-amino alcohol, known as the Wenker synthesis. Like a related class of compounds, they have very high ring strain, making them susceptible to nucleophilic attack. For 10 points, name these nitrogen-containing three-member rings, the aza variants of epoxides.

This empire was divided into four provinces called suyu. The last ruler of this empire was captured after throwing a Bible to the ground before the Battle of Cajamarca. Knotted strings called quipu were used for accounting in this empire and carried by chasqui runners across its extensive road system. Francisco Pizzaro ransomed the last ruler of this empire in exchange for a room filled with gold. Machu Picchu was built as a residence for a ruler of this empire. For 10 points, name this Pre-Columbian empire that dominated the Andes Mountains.

This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for hepatic portal system. It plays a key role in the digestive system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this liver-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The liver is a key component of the Digestive system, involved in hepatic portal system.

An army aiming to retreat to North Carolina after the Battle of Five Forks was eventually trapped at this place two weeks after the Petersburg Campaign ended. A president asked the Marine band to play "Dixie" after an event at this place, where the Army of Northern Virginia was disbanded days after the capture of Richmond. tossups.text: This conflict inspired a Trinidadian trade unionist named Adrian Rienzi to organize a platform of demands against the eventual winner. Three sacks of wedding rings donated by housewives during this conflict allegedly funded the construction of the headquarters of their country's communist party. A failed assassination attempt in the aftermath of this conflict led to the Yekatit 12 massacre. Wilfred Thesiger pointed to the 425 religious officials massacred in Debra Lebanos to reject a satire of sensationalist journalism based on this conflict. A young Anthony Eden failed to prevent this conflict in negotiations following a boundary dispute at an oasis called Walwal. One side's use of chemical weapons at Mekelle during this conflict was announced to the League of Nations in a speech given in Amharic. For 10 points, name this conflict in which Mussolini invaded an African country led by Haile Selassie.

tossups.text: This language was used to write the poem "Manifesto," which declares "The poets have come down from Olympus" and is by the author of Emergency Poems. A poet who wrote in this language spent most of his life exiled in Paris after being framed for arson and wrote, "There are blows in life so powerful... I don't know!" in "The Black Heralds." A poem in this language repeats contradictions, such as "I no longer love her... but maybe I love her" and "I loved her, and sometimes she loved me too." "A Lamp on Earth" titles the first section of a poetry collection in this language, one of whose other poems declares, "Arise to birth with me, my brother!" This is the language of the poem "Tonight I can write the saddest lines," which appears with a "Song of Despair." For 10 points, name this language used to write Canto General by Pablo Neruda.

At one banquet, this man allegedly mistook a fish for a man whose execution he had ordered. This man said of a deceased rival that there "wasn't a bone in this wretched fellow," and this ruler ended the tenure of the anti-pope Laurentius by supporting Symmachus. This king ordered the construction of the Basilica of Saint Apollinaris and patronized the scholar Cassiodorus. After this husband of Audofleda died, his daughter Amalasuntha held power until she was murdered in her bath, and this victor at the battles of Isonzo and Verona also ordered the death of the author of Consolation of Philosophy, Boethius. After winning a campaign at the behest of Emperor Zeno, this man stabbed Odoacer to death at a banquet. For 10 points, name this "great" Ostrogoth king who ruled from Ravenna after the fall of the Roman Empire.

The narrator of one poem by this writer "look'd up in perfect silence at the stars", while in another poem this man "sounds his barbaric yawp." Besides "When I Heard the Learn'd Astronomer" and "Song of Myself", this poet wrote of a man who has "fallen cold and dead" in a poem dedicated to Abraham Lincoln. For 10 points, name this poet of "O Captain! My Captain!" and the collection Leaves of Grass.

This artist cut headlines from the New York Post to create provocative new ones such as "Pope Killed for Freed Hostage." This artist, who stands nude covered in black-and-white paint patterns in an Annie Leibovitz photo, showed a large toothed monster eating a hanged man at the right of one of his murals. His painting of yellow, red, and green figures covering their eyes, ears, and mouth, titled Rebel with Many Causes, deals with the same issue as his work for the group ACT UP. The musical Radiant Baby is about this artist, who painted an orange public mural that uses short black "motion" lines to outline the title three-word message. Many of his works show a large, red heart and characteristic dancing stick figures, while others deal with the AIDS crisis. For 10 points, name this graffiti artist of "Crack is Wack."

Eve and Pierre are brought back to life and given one day to confess love to each other in this author's screenplay The Chips Are Down. After the death of Aegisthus in one play by this author, the title creatures turn into the Furies and torment the citizens of Argos. This author adapted the Oresteia into his play The Flies, and in another of his plays, a valet with no eyelids brings the three main characters into a room with Second Empire furniture. That play by this man includes Estelle attempting to stab Inez with a paper knife and concludes with Garcin stating "Hell is other people." For 10 points, name this French playwright of No Exit.
